correctness.rationale: The source gives the exact increasing thresholds \(A_N\) and the exact equivalence between \(A_N<g\le A_{N+1}\) and having \(N\) positive gaps. With \(x=\phi^{-2N}\), direct Taylor expansion of \((x^{-1}-x)\tan(\pi x/2)\) gives \(g_c-A_N=C_\phi\phi^{-4N}+O(\phi^{-8N})\) with \(C_\phi>0\). Consecutive deficits therefore have ratio \(\phi^{-4}(1+O(\phi^{-4N}))\). The exact interval inequalities then sandwich \(g_c-g\) between two consecutive deficits and yield the logarithmic counting law. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof; the packaged computation is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The source theorem is designed to realize any prescribed finite number of gaps and has a distinguished transition from finitely many to infinitely many gaps. Quantifying how its exact thresholds accumulate is therefore a natural structural question. The geometric ratio \(\phi^{-4}\) and the logarithmic divergence coefficient \(1/(4\log\phi)\) turn the discrete threshold list into a critical scaling law and expose how the golden-mean arithmetic controls approach to the infinite-gap boundary. This is more informative than another isolated threshold value or a routine numerical refinement.
